title: Obesity management (adult)
subject: endocrinology
setting: Outpatient, primary care, obesity and diabetes clinic
summary: Measure BMI and waist-to-height ratio (lower BMI cut-offs for South Asian and other Asian adults), screen for complications, offer structured lifestyle support with a 500 to 750 kcal/day deficit, add semaglutide 2.4 mg or tirzepatide weekly when indicated and continue long term, and refer for metabolic surgery by BMI and comorbidity criteria.

sections.title: Assess and classify
items: BMI (NICE): overweight 25 to 29.9, obesity class 1 30 to 34.9, class 2 35 to 39.9, class 3 40 kg/m2 or more. South Asian, Chinese, other Asian, Middle Eastern, Black African or African-Caribbean adults: overweight 23 to 27.4, obesity 27.5 kg/m2 or more.
Measure waist-to-height ratio when BMI is below 35: 0.4 to 0.49 healthy, 0.5 to 0.59 increased and 0.6 or more high central adiposity. Advise keeping the waist below half the height.

Interpret BMI with caution with high muscle mass and over 65. AACE 2025 treats obesity as adiposity-based chronic disease: diagnose by anthropometry plus complications and set treatment goals by complications, not BMI alone.

Screen for complications: prediabetes and type 2 diabetes (HbA1c or fasting glucose), hypertension, dyslipidaemia, fatty liver (MASLD), obstructive sleep apnoea, PCOS, osteoarthritis, reflux, depression and binge eating.

Look for contributing causes: hypothyroidism, Cushing syndrome if features suggest it, and weight-promoting drugs (antipsychotics, glucocorticoids, insulin, sulfonylureas, some antidepressants and antiepileptics); minimise these where possible (ADA).

sections.title: Lifestyle and weight goals
items: Use person-first, non-judgemental language, ask permission before weighing and weigh in private (ADA).
Any sustained weight loss helps: 5 to 7% improves glycaemia and cardiovascular risk factors; more than 10% brings further benefit, including possible remission of type 2 diabetes (ADA).
Structured programme: 16 or more sessions over 6 months targeting a 500 to 750 kcal/day energy deficit, using an eating pattern that suits the person's culture, preferences and budget.

Physical activity: build up to at least 150 minutes per week of moderate activity plus muscle strengthening; 200 to 300 minutes per week, monthly contact and weekly self-monitoring help maintain weight loss (ADA).
Very-low-calorie diets (800 to 1,000 kcal/day) only under trained supervision with close monitoring and a maintenance plan. Weight-loss supplements are ineffective.

sections.title: Medicines
items: Consider medicines with lifestyle support at BMI 30 kg/m2 or more, or 27 or more with a weight-related complication (licensed thresholds); use thresholds about 2.5 kg/m2 lower in Asian and other high-risk ethnic groups (NICE).
Preferred: semaglutide 2.4 mg or tirzepatide once weekly, which give the greatest weight loss and weight-independent cardiometabolic benefits (ADA 2026).

Titrate slowly to limit nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea: semaglutide 0.25 mg weekly, increasing every 4 weeks through 0.5, 1 and 1.7 mg to 2.4 mg; tirzepatide 2.5 mg weekly for 4 weeks, then increase by 2.5 mg at least 4 weeks apart to a maintenance of 5, 10 or 15 mg.
Individualise the dose (the best dose may be below the maximum) and continue long term after goals are met: stopping usually causes weight regain (ADA).
NICE: with less than 5% weight loss after 6 months (at the highest tolerated dose), review whether to continue; semaglutide is funded within specialist weight services, usually for up to 2 years.
Other options: liraglutide 3 mg daily, orlistat 120 mg three times daily with fat-containing meals, and, where licensed, phentermine-topiramate or naltrexone-bupropion.
With type 2 diabetes, prefer glucose-lowering drugs that also reduce weight (GLP-1 RA, tirzepatide, SGLT2 inhibitors).

sections.title: Safety and special groups
items: GLP-1 based drugs: do not use with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2; avoid with high pancreatitis risk and stop if pancreatitis is suspected. Watch for dehydration and AKI with GI losses, and gallstones.

Not for use in pregnancy: advise effective contraception and stop semaglutide at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy. Tirzepatide reduces oral contraceptive reliability: use a non-oral method or add a barrier method for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose increase.
Aspiration risk under anaesthesia and sedation from delayed gastric emptying: follow local peri-procedure guidance on withholding doses.
When starting in diabetes, reduce insulin or sulfonylurea doses to avoid hypoglycaemia, and review antihypertensives as weight falls.
Protect lean mass with adequate protein, micronutrients and resistance exercise during rapid weight loss.
India: consensus statements use central obesity cut-offs of waist 90 cm or more in men and 80 cm or more in women, and BMI thresholds at least as low as the NICE Asian values.

sections.title: Metabolic and bariatric surgery
items: NICE: refer for specialist assessment at BMI 40 kg/m2 or more, or 35 to 39.9 with a condition likely to improve (type 2 diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, MASLD, obstructive sleep apnoea, idiopathic intracranial hypertension), if the person accepts lifelong follow up.
Expedited assessment for recent-onset type 2 diabetes (within 10 years): offer at BMI 35 or more, consider at 30 to 34.9; lower each threshold by 2.5 kg/m2 in Asian and other high-risk ethnic groups.
ADA 2026: consider metabolic surgery in type 2 diabetes with BMI 30 kg/m2 or more (27.5 or more in Asian people) in good surgical candidates, in high-volume centres.

After surgery: lifelong monitoring of micronutrients (iron, vitamin B12, folate, calcium, vitamin D), mental health and post-bariatric hypoglycaemia; review for weight regain every 6 to 12 months and add medicines if needed.

sections.title: Follow up
items: Measure weight and waist at least yearly, and every 3 months during active treatment (ADA).
Review at 3 and 6 months: weight change, blood pressure, HbA1c, lipids, liver tests, side effects and adherence.
Insufficient response: intensify with a structured programme, another or additional medicine, or metabolic surgery.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Using BMI 30 as the obesity cut-off in South Asian patients, whose cardiometabolic risk starts at lower BMI.
Stopping effective medicines once the target is reached, leading to regain.
Starting GLP-1 based drugs without contraception advice in women who could become pregnant.
Overlooking weight-promoting drugs and untreated complications such as sleep apnoea or depression.
Escalating GLP-1 doses too fast, causing vomiting, dehydration and AKI.

drugs.name: Semaglutide (weight management)
drugs.dose: 0.25 mg SC once weekly for 4 weeks, then 0.5 mg, 1 mg and 1.7 mg each for 4 weeks, then 2.4 mg once weekly maintenance
drugs.notes: Delay escalation if not tolerated. Stop at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy.

drugs.name: Tirzepatide
drugs.dose: 2.5 mg SC once weekly for 4 weeks, then 5 mg; increase by 2.5 mg steps at least 4 weeks apart; maintenance 5, 10 or 15 mg once weekly (maximum 15 mg)
drugs.notes: 2.5 mg is a starting dose only. Reduces oral contraceptive efficacy for 4 weeks after starting and each increase.

drugs.name: Liraglutide (weight management)
drugs.dose: 0.6 mg SC once daily, increased by 0.6 mg weekly to 3 mg once daily
drugs.notes: NICE: stop after 12 weeks on 3 mg if less than 5% weight loss.

drugs.name: Orlistat
drugs.dose: 120 mg orally three times daily with each main meal containing fat
drugs.notes: Stop after 12 weeks if less than 5% weight loss. Add a contraceptive method if severe diarrhoea.
